title: Two Pointers: Overview
summary: Use two pointers starting at opposite ends of a sorted array to find pairs that meet criteria in O(n) time.

sections.heading: The Core Idea
sections.body:
The **two-pointer technique** uses two pointers that start at opposite ends of a **sorted array** and gradually move towards each other.

Instead of checking all O(n²) pairs with nested loops, we eliminate unnecessary pairs by leveraging the sorted property. Each pointer movement eliminates multiple pairs from consideration, reducing time complexity to **O(n)**.

The pointers represent the **current pair** being considered. Based on how the current pair compares to our target, we move one pointer to eliminate all pairs that can't possibly work.

sections.heading: How It Works: Two Sum Example
sections.body:
Given a sorted array `[1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 13]` and `target = 13`:

1. Initialize `left = 0`, `right = len(nums) - 1`
2. Calculate `current_sum = nums[left] + nums[right]`
3. If `current_sum == target`: **found it!**
4. If `current_sum > target`: move `right` pointer left (all pairs with current right are too large)
5. If `current_sum < target`: move `left` pointer right (all pairs with current left are too small)
6. Repeat until pointers meet or pair is found

This works because the array is **sorted** - if a sum is too large, every pair involving larger numbers will also be too large.

sections.heading: Pattern Variants
sections.body:
**Opposite Ends** (most common)
- Pointers start at `0` and `len(nums) - 1`
- Move toward each other based on comparison logic
- Used for: pair sum, triplet sum, container with most water

**Same Direction / Fast-Slow**
- Both pointers start at the beginning
- One moves faster than the other
- Used for: removing duplicates, partitioning arrays, cycle detection

sections.heading: When to Use Two Pointers
sections.body:
Consider this technique when you see:
- **Sorted array** (or can be sorted)
- Searching for **pairs or triplets** meeting criteria
- Problems involving **comparing elements** from opposite ends
- Need to **reduce O(n²) to O(n)** by eliminating pairs

Common problem types: pair sum, triplet sum, container problems, partitioning, removing elements.

approach: Input array is sorted (or can be sorted without violating constraints)
Need to find pairs/triplets that satisfy a condition (sum, product, difference)
Naive nested loop solution would be O(n²)
Can eliminate multiple candidates based on sorted property
Problem involves comparing elements from opposite ends or tracking regions

quiz.q: At any point during the two-pointer search for Two Sum, what do the positions of the two pointers represent?
options: The pairs that have already been eliminated
The smallest and largest values seen so far
The pair of numbers currently being considered
The bounds of the portion of the array that is already sorted
quiz.explain: The two pointers always represent the current pair being evaluated. When we move a pointer, we're eliminating all pairs involving the old position and moving to the next candidate pair.

quiz.q: Why does the two-pointer technique require the array to be sorted?
options: To ensure the algorithm runs in O(n log n) time
To guarantee that moving a pointer eliminates multiple pairs based on comparison logic
To allow binary search within the two-pointer loop
To prevent infinite loops when pointers meet
quiz.explain: The sorted property lets us reason about entire groups of pairs at once. If current sum is too large, we know ALL pairs with the current right value are too large, so we can eliminate them by moving right pointer left.
